articles.title: Happy Karwa Chauth 2026: Images, Wishes, Messages, Quotes, Pictures and Greeting Cards
articles.summary: Karwa Chauth is a festival you can see, smell and hear before it even begins.
articles.body: Karwa Chauth is a festival you can see, smell and hear before it even begins. There is the henna drying on palms, the jingle of new bangles, the aroma of sargi in the pre-dawn kitchen, and the long, quiet wait for the moon. Greetings pour in from mothers-in-law, sisters, friends and colleagues, along with a flood of pictures and cards. Karwa Chauth falls on Thursday, October 29, 2026, in India, with moonrise in Delhi in the evening at around 8:17 pm. Puja and moonrise timings vary by city, and some calendars list October 28, so please check your local panchang. If you want your greetings to feel heartfelt rather than forwarded, here is a collection of wishes, messages, quotes and picture ideas that you can use as they are or tweak with a name and a memory of your own.Heartfelt wishes for everyoneThese all-purpose greetings suit relatives, neighbours and friends. Adding the person’s name makes a simple line feel far more personal, so take a moment to do it.Wishing you a blessed Karwa Chauth filled with love, patience and happiness.May Karwa Mata bless you and your family with health, joy and togetherness.Happy Karwa Chauth! May the moon light up your life tonight.May your fast be easy and your prayers be answered.Warm wishes to you and your loved ones on this beautiful festival.May every moonrise bring more love into your home.Messages for a loved oneKarwa Chauth is about a bond, so these messages work best when they are personal. Many couples now fast together or mark the day with a small surprise, and a thank-you can mean more than a perfect poem.Thank you for being my partner, my friend and my biggest support.Fasting is easy when your smile is waiting at the end of the day.May our love grow stronger with every Karwa Chauth. Happy Karwa Chauth, my love!Happy Karwa Chauth to the woman who holds our home together with love.I may not keep the fast, but I will keep you smiling today.To wives: Your devotion and strength inspire me every day. Thank you for everything.Messages for mothers-in-law and eldersIn many homes, the day begins with sargi lovingly prepared by the mother-in-law. A respectful, affectionate message is a lovely way to say thank you.Thank you for the sargi, the blessings and the love. Happy Karwa Chauth, Maa.Your guidance makes every festival in our home special.Please bless us today and always. Wishing you good health and happiness.Touching your feet in my heart. May your blessings stay with our family.To our elders: Your prayers carry us through every year.Wishing you a peaceful, joyful and blessed Karwa Chauth.Wishes for friends and sistersFriends and sisters turn the day into a celebration, with matching outfits, mehendi sessions and group photos. Keep these light, cheerful and a little cheeky.Happy Karwa Chauth to my favourite partner in mehendi and gossip!May your fast be easy, your henna be dark and your selfies be perfect.Thank you for being the friend who makes every festival brighter.Sister, you are already glowing! May tonight’s moon be as bright as your smile.Let’s survive the day, eat well tonight and take a hundred photos.Dress up, shine on and enjoy every moment with me.Sargi and early-morning wishesThe day begins before sunrise, and a kind message at that hour shows you are thinking of the person observing the fast.Good morning and happy Karwa Chauth! Eat well and stay strong today.May the sargi give you all the energy you need to complete your fast.Drink plenty of water now and keep your spirits high.Wishing you a calm, happy and blessed day ahead.May Karwa Mata give you patience and strength from sunrise to moonrise.Sending love and good wishes as you begin your day.Moonrise and evening messagesThe evening is the emotional highlight, with the thali, the karwa, the sieve and the wait for the moon. These lines are perfect for sharing just before moonrise.The moon is almost here! Happy Karwa Chauth, and may your wait be worth it.May the moon shine on your love and fill your life with light.Time to dress up, light the diya and look for the moon.May your prayers be heard and your fast be fulfilled tonight.Break your fast with a smile, a sip of water and a grateful heart.Wishing you a joyful evening with the people you love.Quotes and thoughts for the dayThese short reflections suit captions and status updates, especially beside a photo of a decorated thali, a hand with mehendi or the moon.Love is not only said, it is also kept, like a fast and a promise.Faith and patience make even the longest day feel short.The moon appears in its own time, and so does everything we wait for.A relationship grows on small acts of care, day after day.True devotion is quiet, steady and full of love.Some of the best moments come after the longest waits.Short lines for WhatsApp and InstagramNot everyone has time for a long message, and sometimes a few words say it best. These short lines fit neatly over pictures without hiding the artwork.Happy Karwa Chauth!Fast, faith and festivity.Moon, mehendi and magic.Waiting for the moon, wishing for love.Dressed up, fasting on, hearts full.Love, light and a little patience.Picking the right images, pictures and greeting cardsA good picture lifts any message, while a cluttered one can spoil it. A little care goes a long way, especially on small phone screens.Choose clear, high-quality pictures of a decorated puja thali, a diya, mehendi, bangles or the moon.Pick warm festive colours like red, maroon, gold and green.Keep the text short and the font easy to read.Prefer a simple background over a busy template.Make your own card using a photo of your thali, your mehendi or a couple photo with your partner’s permission.Use only images you own or that are free to share.Sharing wishes with sincerityThe best greeting is the one that sounds like you. A little thought turns a forwarded message into something the other person will remember.Change a word or two and add the person’s name.Mention something you share, like last year’s mehendi session or a favourite sargi recipe.Avoid sending the same forward to every group.Send wishes at a reasonable hour, and keep early-morning messages short.Be mindful of people who celebrate differently or are not observing the fast.Call an elder or send a voice note. articles.title: Citing diversion of staff from relief work, Maharashtra govt puts off cooperative society polls in all 304 drought-hit talukas
articles.summary: Maharashtra postpones cooperative society elections in 304 drought-hit talukas to avoid diverting staff from relief work; housing and court-ordered polls exempt.
articles.body: Mumbai: The state govt late on Tuesday indefinitely postponed elections for all eligible cooperative societies in the 304 talukas hit by drought, citing the need to prevent the diversion of administrative staff from relief work and inconvenience to farmers and others affected by the crisis.But cooperative housing societies, societies whose elections have been ordered by Supreme Court or Bombay high court, and those where the nomination process had begun before Tuesday have been exempted, according to a govt resolution (GR) issued by the state cooperation department.The state had seen feverish preparations for these elections over the past few months. All district central cooperative banks, which are considered the financial power centres of taluka and district politics, were scheduled to go to the polls, as were around 5,000 cooperative societies, like cooperative sugar factories, credit unions, cooperative banks, spinning mills, market committees and marketing associations. Last week, Rajarshi Shahu Shetkari Samavichari Aghadi, backed by Congress MLC Satej Patil, won the Kolhapur District Cooperative Milk Producers Federation polls with 13 seats, defeating the Mahayuti-supported Chhatrapati Shahu Shetkari Vikas Aghadi, led by senior NCP minister Hasan Mushrif, which secured 12 seats.The GR said owing to the drought situation in the 304 talukas, it is necessary to immediately implement various relief measures. “For this, additional administrative responsibility has been created on the revenue, agriculture, animal husbandry, cooperation, rural development, water supply, water conservation and other related departments. In such a situation, if the election process of cooperative societies in these talukas is continued, there is a possibility that govt officials/employees will get involved in the election process, which is likely to affect the drought relief work. Also, it is likely that it will be inconvenient for farmers and members of the drought-affected areas to participate in the election process of cooperative societies at the present time,” it said.The department invoked Section 73CC of Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act, 1960, which empowers the state govt to defer cooperative elections during natural calamities and other exceptional circumstances.The state govt has announced relief measures for the 304 talukas. These include crop loan restructuring, suspension of agricultural loan recoveries, waivers on current electricity bills for agricultural pumps, provision of drinking water via tankers, fodder availability for livestock, and expanded employment under the employment guarantee scheme. articles.title: Bengal’s new industry policy may fast-track projects over 100 acres
articles.summary: Bengal’s new industry policy, to be unveiled Nov 5, aims to fast-track clearances for 100+ acre projects, tighten land-use rules and add investor incentives.
articles.body: Kolkata: Bengal’s new industry policy is expected to fast-track clearances for industrial projects requiring more than 100 acres and impose stricter conditions on land use. Chief minister Suvendu Adhikari will unveil the policy on Nov 5.The state cabinet approved the policy on Wednesday after incorporating recommendations from ministers. Industry captains have been invited to Nabanna for the launch.“The industry policy was discussed at the previous cabinet meeting. Recommendations from two ministers who were part of the Group of Ministers constituted to frame the policy were incorporated,” Adhikari said, crediting finance minister Swapan Dasgupta and industry minister Tapas Roy. “I have not interfered much in the formulation of the policy,” he added.According to Nabanna sources, the policy is expected to offer incentives to investors, streamline industrial clearances through a single-window system and introduce conditions governing the allocation and use of land for industrial projects.Govt is also considering a provision requiring industries to begin production within three years of receiving land, failing which allotments could be cancelled and land reclaimed. The final provisions will be known when the policy is formally unveiled.The policy is expected to be a key component of BJP govt’s efforts to improve Bengal’s investment climate and attract large-scale industrial projects.Adhikari also announced that financial assistance under Mukhyamantri Kisan Samman Nidhi, renamed from the earlier Krishak Bandhu scheme, would be transferred to farmers on Nov 5. He will initiate the transfer at a programme in Pursurah, Hooghly, which is expected to cover more than 50 lakh registered farmers.The cabinet also directed the finance department to release the next instalment of budgetary funds to administrative departments that have spent at least 70% of their allocations on public welfare schemes.It also approved observance of Janjatiya Gaurav Divas across Bengal from Nov 11 to 18 to commemorate the birth anniversary of tribal freedom fighter Birsa Munda.InsetState clears 1,200 posts across five departmentsThe state govt has approved around 1,200 new posts across five departments, chief minister Suvendu Adhikari said on Wednesday. The posts have been approved in animal resources development, urban development and municipal affairs, health and family welfare, fire and emergency services, and home and hill affairs. “We will issue recruitment notifications soon and conduct examinations through PSC and SSC to fill these posts,” Adhikari said.He added that the state cabinet had approved around 45,000 posts at its previous meeting. articles.title: Sandalwood theft up, call for inquiry gets louder
articles.summary: Sandalwood theft rises in Palakkad’s Nenmara division as nine trees are felled in Thekkady; trust urges independent inquiry, case review and accountability.
articles.body: Palakkad: Heavy rain may have provided cover for the theft of sandalwood trees from the Thekkady forest station limits under the Kollengode forest range on Sunday.The forest department has registered a case after nine sandalwood trees were found to have felled in Vattayarmadakku forest, which comes under Nenmara forest division near Tamil Nadu border.Range officer V Unnikrishnan said the stolen timber may have been transported across the border into TN. Residents of a colony adjoining the forest are also under the scanner as part of the investigation.A detailed inspection carried out on Wednesday found that of the nine felled trees, six had been removed while two were abandoned because they lacked heartwood, according to forest officials.The incident has triggered concerns over repeated sandalwood thefts and illegal tree felling in the Nenmara forest division.Around 30 sandalwood trees have been reportedly stolen from Vamala and Thekkady in the past two months. In another incident, about 25 trees, including five sandalwood trees, were allegedly felled at Kottamala last week.The last sandalwood theft case registered at Thekkady forest station was in 2024, when 21 trees were stolen, Unnikrishnan said.Animals and Nature Ethics Community trust has urged the state govt to order an independent, time-bound inquiry into the incidents. It has sought a review of sandalwood theft cases registered over the past five years, scrutiny of forest patrol records and accountability for any established lapses.The organisation has also called for an investigation into an earlier tree-felling incident at Vattayarmadakku, during which some forest personnel were reportedly suspended around two years ago.The trust has demanded a written action-taken report detailing investigation progress, recoveries and arrests.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kochi | Silver Rate in Kochi | Bank Holidays in Kochi | Public Holidays in KochiStay updated with the latest Kochi news. articles.summary: medium nocaption When evaluating West Asian foreign policy and geopolitical balances, viewing political actors and states as monolithic, homogeneous blocs
articles.body: When evaluating West Asian foreign policy and geopolitical balances, viewing political actors and states as monolithic, homogeneous blocs is a profound mistake. To accurately decode the complex aftermath of Israel’s elections, and region’s trajectory, particularly the Iran-Israel conflict, this superficial lens needs to be discarded.At the time of going to print, there were no clear winners in the election that saw a historic turnout. Netanyahu’s rightwing bloc is ahead of its centrist rival, Eisenkot’s bloc, but without a majority. But what is abundantly clear is the phenomenal rise of Arab parties, whose strong showing cannot be overlooked during govt formation. This will be a complex affair of coalition politics, in Israel’s proportional representation system, that gives parties seats basis vote shares. The Arab parties are projected to win at least 17 seats in the 120-seat Knesset.
